composio.note: Composio lists Gmail under 'Composio-managed OAuth available', so you can ship on the managed app and skip Google verification entirely. Bring your own app only for your own branding on the consent screen, scopes the managed app does not request, or your own quota. For your own app, copy the redirect URI shown in the Composio dashboard when creating the auth config; Composio docs currently show three different values (v1/auth-apps/add, v3/toolkits/auth/callback, v3.1/toolkits/auth/callback).

summary: Creating the OAuth client takes under an hour, but almost every useful Gmail scope (read, modify, compose, metadata) is classified restricted. Going to production for external users means brand verification, restricted-scope review with a demo video, and an annual third-party CASA security assessment if Gmail data touches your servers, which it does when Composio stores tokens and proxies calls. Plan for weeks, not days, and recurring yearly cost.
difficultyReason: Restricted scopes trigger the heaviest review Google has: brand verification, Limited Use compliance, scope justification, demo video, and a paid annual CASA assessment by a Google-empanelled lab. Only gmail.send is merely sensitive.

time.notes: Hands-on: 1-2 hours to create the client and test; 1-3 days (inferred) to prepare homepage, privacy policy, domain verification, justification and demo video for review. Approval: Brand verification 2-3 business days (source); restricted-scope review plus CASA 'several weeks' per Google, typically 4-12 weeks end to end (inferred). To production: Immediately for up to 100 test users in Testing mode; roughly 1-3 months (inferred) for unrestricted external users with restricted Gmail scopes.

review.details: Gmail scopes https://mail.google.com/, gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose, gmail.insert, gmail.metadata, gmail.settings.basic and gmail.settings.sharing are restricted; gmail.send is sensitive; gmail.labels is non-sensitive. Restricted scopes require brand verification (domain ownership in Search Console, homepage, privacy policy on the same domain), a scope justification, a demo video, Limited Use compliance, and, if restricted data is stored on or passes through a server, a CASA security assessment by a Google-empanelled assessor resulting in a Letter of Validation. Reassessment is required at least every 12 months. Exempt: Internal user type (your own Workspace org only), personal use, and apps still in development/testing.

limitsBeforeApproval: Testing status: max 100 test users you list by email, a warning screen before consent, and authorizations (including refresh tokens) expire 7 days after consent, so Composio connections silently break weekly. Publishing to In production without verification shows the 'Google hasn't verified this app' screen and caps the app at 100 new users in total until verified.

prerequisites.item: Google account with access to Google Cloud console and a Cloud project
prerequisites.why: The OAuth client and consent screen live in a Cloud project. No billing account is needed to create OAuth clients.

prerequisites.item: A domain you own, verified in Google Search Console by a project Owner or Editor
prerequisites.why: Brand verification requires every authorized domain to be verified.

prerequisites.item: Public homepage on that domain describing the app (not just a login page)
prerequisites.why: Brand verification rejects homepages that do not describe the app or that are login-only.

prerequisites.item: Privacy policy on the same domain, linked from the homepage, covering Google user data and Limited Use
prerequisites.why: Required for brand and restricted-scope verification.
Must show the OAuth flow with client ID in the address bar, the consent screen in English, and each restricted scope in use.
Third-party lab fee, paid by the developer, renewed yearly. Not priced by Google.
Internal user type skips verification but only lets users in your own org connect.

steps.title: Pick scopes and check classification
steps.detail: List the Gmail actions your agent needs and map each to the narrowest scope. Use gmail.send (sensitive) alone if the agent only sends; anything that reads or drafts mail is restricted. Every scope must be justified as least privilege.

steps.title: Create a Cloud project and enable the Gmail API
steps.detail: In Google Cloud console create or select a project, then APIs & Services > Library > Gmail API > Enable.

steps.title: Configure Google Auth Platform branding and audience
steps.detail: Enter app name, support email, logo (optional), homepage, privacy policy and ToS links, authorized domains, developer contact. Choose External (or Internal for single-Workspace use). An agent can draft all field values; a human must submit.

steps.title: Declare scopes on the Data Access page
steps.detail: Add exactly the scopes you will request. Mismatches between code and the consent screen trigger the unverified-app warning.

steps.title: Create a Web application OAuth client
steps.detail: Clients > Create client > Web application. Paste the redirect URI copied from the Composio auth-config screen into Authorized redirect URIs. Copy the client ID and secret.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config
steps.detail: Composio dashboard > Create Auth Config > Gmail > OAuth2 > use your own developer credentials. Paste client ID, secret, and scopes. Confirm the redirect URI there matches the GCP client byte for byte.

steps.title: Add test users and run a test connection
steps.detail: Audience > Test users: add up to 100 accounts. Connect one through Composio and call a Gmail tool. Expect re-auth after 7 days while in Testing.

steps.title: Prepare homepage, privacy policy and Limited Use disclosure
steps.detail: Draft privacy-policy text covering how Google user data is accessed, used, stored, shared and deleted, plus the Limited Use statement. Check homepage links the policy and is on the verified domain.

steps.title: Write scope justifications and demo-video script
steps.detail: Draft per-scope justification (why narrower scopes fail) and a shot list: consent screen with correct app name, client ID visible in the URL bar, English consent language, each scope's feature in use. Developer records and uploads as Unlisted on YouTube.

steps.title: Verify domain and submit for verification
steps.detail: Verify the domain in Search Console, publish the app (In production), and submit from the Verification Center. Google emails project Owners/Editors.

steps.title: Google review and CASA assessment
steps.detail: Google reviews branding and scope use, then Trust and Safety contacts you to start CASA (tier AL1 or AL2 by risk). You engage an empanelled lab, fix findings, and obtain a Letter of Validation.

steps.title: Calendar annual recertification
steps.detail: Reassessment is due at least every 12 months from LOA approval; adding a new restricted scope can trigger it early.

nuances.title: 7-day token expiry in Testing
nuances.detail: Any non-identity scope in Testing status makes authorizations expire 7 days after consent. Fine for a demo, not for a running agent.

nuances.title: gmail.send is only sensitive
nuances.detail: A send-only agent avoids CASA: sensitive scopes need brand verification, justification and demo video, but no security assessment.

nuances.title: CASA is triggered by server-side handling
nuances.detail: Required when restricted data is stored on or transmitted through servers. Using your client with Composio means tokens and Gmail data pass through Composio's backend, so assume CASA applies.

nuances.title: 100 new users lifetime cap when unverified
nuances.detail: Unverified production apps showing the warning are capped at 100 new users in total until verified.

nuances.title: Brand verification result expires
nuances.detail: A compliant brand verification result is valid for 7 days; publish within that window or re-verify.

nuances.title: 100 refresh tokens per account per client
nuances.detail: Each Google account can hold 100 refresh tokens per client ID; the 101st silently invalidates the oldest. Avoid reconnecting the same test account repeatedly.

nuances.title: AI training needs explicit consent
nuances.detail: If Gmail data is used to train models, the demo video must show explicit user consent for it; Limited Use otherwise restricts such use.

blockers.problem: Homepage is a login page or on a different domain than the privacy policy
blockers.whatToDo: Publish a public product page on the verified domain that links the same privacy policy used on the consent screen.

blockers.problem: Requested scopes broader than features shown
blockers.whatToDo: Drop to the narrowest scope (e.g. gmail.send or gmail.readonly instead of mail.google.com) and show every scope's feature in the video.

blockers.problem: Demo video missing client ID in URL bar or non-English consent screen
blockers.whatToDo: Re-record with the full OAuth flow, browser address bar visible, consent screen in English.
Fix the lab's findings and resubmit; budget engineering time for this.
Keep project Owner/Editor contacts current; Google warns ignored notices can cost API access.

agentCanDo: Map agent features to the narrowest Gmail scopes and report their classification
Draft privacy policy and Limited Use disclosure text
Draft homepage copy describing the app's Gmail functionality
Write per-scope justifications for the verification form
Write the demo-video script and shot list
Pre-fill consent-screen field values (name, links, domains)
Check the redirect URI in GCP matches the Composio auth config exactly
Prepare a CASA readiness checklist and track recertification dates
developerMustDo: Own the Google account and Cloud project and click through console screens
Verify domain ownership in Google Search Console
Publish homepage and privacy policy on the owned domain
Record and upload the demo video
Submit verification and respond to Google's emails
Contract and pay a CASA assessor, remediate findings, and recertify yearly
redirectUri: Must exactly match an authorized redirect URI (scheme, case, trailing slash). HTTPS required except localhost and loopback IPs. No raw IPs other than loopback, no wildcards, no fragments, no userinfo, no path traversal, TLD must be on the public suffix list, googleusercontent.com not allowed. Copy Composio's value from the auth-config screen.

claims.claim: gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.compose, gmail.insert, gmail.metadata, gmail.settings.* and https://mail.google.com/ are restricted; gmail.send is sensitive; gmail.labels is non-sensitive.
Testing status allows up to 100 test users and authorizations expire 7 days after consent unless only basic identity scopes are requested.
Unverified apps showing the unverified-app screen are limited to 100 new users in total until verified.
Restricted-scope apps that store or transmit restricted data on servers need a CASA assessment by a Google-empanelled assessor, renewed at least every 12 months.
Brand verification typically takes 2-3 business days and restricted-scope verification can take several weeks.
Brand verification requires a verified domain, a non-login homepage, and a privacy policy on the same domain.
Internal user type, personal use, and dev/testing apps are exempt from verification.
Redirect URIs must be HTTPS (localhost excepted), exact match, with no wildcards or fragments.
Composio offers a managed Gmail OAuth app.
CASA Tier 2 from TAC Security is listed around USD 540 per app per year; other labs quote USD 3,000-4,500.
Using your own client with Composio means Gmail data passes through a third-party server, so CASA applies.
End-to-end time to production with restricted Gmail scopes is roughly 1-3 months.

openQuestions: Composio docs show three redirect URIs (https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add on composio.dev/auth/googleapps, .../api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback on the custom-auth-configs page, .../api/v3.1/toolkits/auth/callback in programmatic examples). Developers should copy the value from the dashboard; which is canonical is unconfirmed.
Google publishes no fixed SLA for restricted-scope review; the 1-3 month total is inferred.
CASA pricing comes from vendor pages, not Google, and may have changed.
Whether CASA tier (AL1 vs AL2) for a Composio-backed agent would be lower is decided per app by Google.
Workspace admins in customer orgs can block unconfigured third-party apps regardless of verification; not covered in the pages fetched.
